Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The invention relates to a filter device with a filter element (1) which can be received in a filter housing that consists of at least two interconnectable housing parts (17, 19). The filter element (1) can be fixed to a housing part (19) in a removable manner by means of a screw connection (32, 33), and an additional screw connection (17, 41) is provided for connecting the housing parts (17, 19). The invention is characterized in that in order to transmit a torque between threaded elements (33) of the screw connection (32, 33) and of the additional screw connection (41), said threaded elements being rotatable relative to each other, a coupling device (43, 46, 61) is added which allows an additional rotational movement of the threaded element (17) of the additional screw connection (41) when the threaded element (33) of the screw connection (32, 33) reaches the fixed rotational state.

The invention relates to a filter device comprising a filter element that can be arranged inside a filter housing. The filter housing is formed from at least two housing parts that can be connected to one another. This construction allows the filter housing to be opened, for example in order to insert, replace, or service the filter element, and then closed again for operation.

The filter element is designed so that it can be removably fixed to one of the housing parts by means of a screw connection. This screw connection enables the filter element to be securely held in position during use, while still allowing it to be detached when necessary, such as during maintenance or replacement.

In addition to the screw connection used to secure the filter element, a further screw connection is provided for connecting the housing parts to each other. This additional screw connection ensures that the housing parts can be joined together reliably and tightly, thereby forming the filter housing around the filter element.

A coupling device is arranged between the threaded elements of the two screw connections. These threaded elements are capable of rotating relative to each other. The coupling device serves to transmit torque between them, so that rotation applied during assembly can be used both to fix the filter element and to connect the housing parts.

The coupling device is configured in such a way that, once the threaded element associated with the screw connection for the filter element has reached its fixed or tightened position, the threaded element of the additional screw connection can continue to rotate. As a result, the housing parts can still be tightened together even after the filter element has been securely fixed. This enables reliable mounting of the filter element and proper closure of the filter housing without overloading or further rotating the already-fixed filter element connection.
outputs.L4:
A filter device is proposed which comprises a filter housing made up of at least two housing parts and a filter element arranged inside the housing. The filter element is designed to be replaceable and is removably secured to one of the housing parts by means of a screw connection. The two housing parts themselves are also connected to one another by a further screw connection. In order to ensure reliable assembly and disassembly, the device includes a coupling arrangement which controls the transmission of torque between threaded components that can rotate relative to one another.

In such a filter device, the filter element may first be screwed onto a receiving portion of one housing part until it reaches a defined fixed or sealing position. This connection can ensure, for example, that the filter element is held securely and that fluid flowing through the housing is properly guided through the filter medium rather than bypassing it. After this fixed state has been reached, however, continued rotation may still be required in order to fully close the housing by tightening the screw connection between the housing parts. Without a special arrangement, this continued rotation could apply excessive torque to the already-fixed filter element, potentially damaging the filter element, deforming a seal, loosening the filter connection, or impairing the correct functional position of the element.

To avoid these disadvantages, the filter device is provided with a coupling device between the threaded elements involved in the two screw connections. The coupling device allows torque to be transmitted during an initial phase of assembly so that the filter element can be screwed into its proper mounted position. Once the filter-element screw connection has reached its predetermined fixed condition, the coupling permits relative rotation between the associated components. As a result, the housing screw connection can continue to be rotated and tightened without further tightening, overloading, or unintentionally disturbing the connection between the filter element and the housing part.

The coupling device may therefore act as a torque-limiting, slipping, disengaging, or freewheeling connection. It can be configured so that, below a certain resistance or torque threshold, rotational movement is transferred from one threaded element to another. When the filter element reaches its end position and the resistance increases, the coupling can release or slip, allowing the housing parts to continue rotating relative to the filter element. In this way, the assembly process remains simple and can be carried out by rotating one housing part relative to the other, while the filter element is automatically brought into its correct position and then protected against excessive torque.

The additional screw connection between the housing parts can then be tightened independently until the housing is securely closed. Sealing elements may be provided between the housing parts and/or between the filter element and the housing part to prevent leakage and to ensure proper filtration. The arrangement is particularly advantageous because it enables a reliable sequence of assembly: first, the filter element is fixed in its intended operating position; second, the housing parts are fully screwed together; and third, the filter element remains undisturbed despite the further tightening movement required for the housing.

During replacement of the filter element, the same principle may also assist disassembly. When the housing parts are unscrewed, the coupling device can allow controlled transmission or interruption of torque so that the filter element can be removed from its mounting position in a predictable manner. This makes maintenance easier and reduces the risk that the filter element remains stuck in the housing or is damaged during removal.

The proposed filter device thus provides a simple and robust construction in which two screw connections cooperate without interfering with one another. By using the coupling device to manage torque transmission between relatively rotatable threaded elements, the filter element can be securely and removably fixed while the housing can still be completely closed and tightened. The arrangement improves assembly reliability, protects the filter element and sealing surfaces from excessive mechanical load, and ensures a secure and leak-tight operating state of the filter device.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it is also one of the most important. It is called a definite article, and its job is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we might mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word helps make communication clearer. It gives focus, adds meaning, and connects ideas. For example, “the sun,” “the world,” and “the truth” all sound complete and familiar because “the” tells us we are referring to something known or unique.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” appears everywhere in everyday speech and writing. It helps shape sentences and guide understanding. Without it, English would feel less precise and less natural. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a powerful role in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention involving a filter element mounted in a multi-part filter housing with removable screw connections and a torque-transmitting coupling device.
counterfactuals.output: A filter assembly comprises a multi-part filter housing and a filter element received therein, wherein the housing parts are detachably connected to one another by at least one screw connection. The filter element is mounted in the housing such that, during assembly and/or disassembly of the housing, torque can be transmitted between a housing part and the filter element by a torque-transmitting coupling device. The coupling device includes mutually engageable coupling formations provided on the filter element and on an associated housing component, the coupling formations being configured to establish a rotational driving connection while permitting axial insertion and removal of the filter element. By applying torque through the removable screw connection, the filter element can be rotationally positioned, secured, or released in a defined manner within the housing. The arrangement facilitates simple replacement of the filter element, reliable sealing and positioning in the assembled state, and controlled removal of the element when the housing parts are separated.

counterfactuals.output:
A filter device comprises a filter housing having at least two housing parts (17, 19) which delimit an interior for receiving a filter element. The housing parts (17, 19) are detachably connected to one another by a screw connection (32, 33), such that the housing can be opened for replacement of the filter element and closed in a fluid-tight manner during operation.

At least one of the housing parts (17) is further provided with a fastening screw connection (17, 41), by means of which the filter device can be mounted on, or connected to, a receiving component, in particular a fluid-carrying assembly. The screw connection (32, 33) between the housing parts (17, 19) and the fastening screw connection (17, 41) may have different thread directions and/or thread pitches.

In order to permit reliable mounting and dismantling, the filter device further comprises a coupling device (43, 46, 61) configured to transmit torque between associated components of the filter device. The coupling device (43, 46, 61) is arranged such that, during rotational actuation of one housing part (19), torque can be transmitted selectively or positively to another component, in particular to the housing part (17) and/or to a threaded fastening part (41). The coupling device may comprise cooperating coupling elements (43, 46) and an actuating or locking element (61), which engage with one another in a rotationally fixed manner at least in one operating state.

By virtue of the coupling device (43, 46, 61), torque applied for opening or closing the screw connection (32, 33) can also be used for tightening or loosening the fastening screw connection (17, 41), or conversely undesired release of one screw connection during actuation of the other can be avoided. The filter device therefore allows simplified installation and servicing while maintaining secure threaded connections and sealing of the housing parts (17, 19).
